# Wardline: Security Landing Page with Animated HUD Art

Implemente a página conforme a demonstração original compilada incluída no pacote. Preserve composição, animações, responsividade e estados interativos. O código-fonte editável e os serviços de backend não foram recuperados nesta captura. Este prompt é uma instrução de reconstrução, não um prompt original do autor.

A light landing page for a security monitoring product, with six animated Illos HUD assets floating on deep night gradients. Hero with live status cards, Detect, Respond and Prove rows, a coverage grid, a numbered response rail, a customer story and pricing. Assets loop while in view and hold still under reduced motion. Plain HTML, CSS and JS built with Vite. More at illos.dev.

See it, stop it, and show your auditor you did.

Most small teams have no one watching at 3 a.m. Wardline does the watching, hands you the next step, and keeps the record.

Detect

Hears the one odd signal in a week of normal.

Wardline learns how your team signs in, ships and works, then flags what breaks the pattern. A login from a new country on an unknown laptop is a page. A teammate on holiday in Lisbon is not.

  • Checks every event against 30 days of history
  • Folds duplicates into one alert
  • Tunes itself as your team grows

Respond

Puts the next step inside the alert.

Every alert arrives with what happened, where, and the first thing to do. Lock the account, revoke the key or take the laptop off the network without opening another tool.

Prove

Keeps the receipts your auditor asks for.

Every alert, every action and who took it goes into a log nobody can edit. When a customer sends a security questionnaire, export the evidence instead of writing it from memory.

  • A tamper-proof log of every action
  • Evidence packs for SOC 2 and ISO 27001
  • Three years of history on Business

Covers the places small teams get hit.

Six checks, all on from the first day. Connect your accounts and Wardline starts with what’s already wrong.

  • Cloud accounts

    Public storage, open ports and admin keys left lying around.

  • Sign-ins

    New countries, impossible travel and password guessing across your single sign-on.

  • Secrets in code

    Keys and tokens pushed to a repository, caught before anyone else finds them.

  • Laptops

    Disk encryption, screen lock and updates on every machine your team uses.

  • Connected apps

    Every app with access to your mail and files, and who let it in.

  • On-call paging

    Phone, text or chat to the right person, and on to the next if nobody answers.

From alert to all clear.

What happens between the first odd signal and the incident closing, with no one refreshing a dashboard.

  1. 1

    Something crosses the line

    A sign-in, a settings change or a new process doesn’t match what’s normal for your team.

  2. 2

    One person gets one page

    Whoever is on call hears about it in under a minute, with what happened and what to do first.

  3. 3

    Contain it from the alert

    Lock, revoke or isolate with one button. Every action can be undone.

  4. 4

    All clear, on the record

    When things settle, the incident closes and lands in your audit log with every step.
